apparatus.basis: Coptic page numeral for 29; transcription shows [ⲕⲟ] but the page sequence requires ⲕⲑ. Likely a transcription artifact (the same letters [ⲕⲟ] also restore the start of ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ in line 1).
Initial letters of ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ; standard Greek loanword 'cosmos.'
Lycopolitan ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ idiom 'out of the cosmos'; cf. preceding ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ.
Definite article required before ⲥⲁⲝⲛⲉ.
Editor's restoration of verb prefix; ϥⲁ-ⲉⲁⲍϥ̄ likely a verbal form 'he carries/draws (him)'; precise verb uncertain.
Greek ἀνδριάς 'statue, image-of-a-man,' fitting ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'depiction' in line 3 (cosmic Statue/Image of the Living Soul). Less likely ἀνδρεία 'courage.'
ⲉⲡⲉ → ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲇⲏ ('since, because'); standard Greek conjunction continued onto next line.
ⲛⲍⲃⲏⲩⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all the things'; ⲛⲍ- = the plural article.
Editor restoration; ⲭⲁ uncertain — possibly Coptic ⲭⲁ 'branch, limb' or contracted abode-noun. Function parallels ⲥⲱⲙⲁ as identifier of the entity's outer aspect.
ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ idiom 'stands fast/firm.'
Completes ⲧⲉⲧϩⲁⲙⲁ[ⲍⲉ ⲛⲍⲏⲧⲥ] = 'which-grasps within it (i.e. the wreath).'
Definite article ⲧ- before feminine ⲛⲁⲟ ⲛⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'great fire.' One letter visible trace before.
Relative converter ⲧⲉⲧ- before future ⲛⲁⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄.
Editor restoration; completes ⲡ[ⲱⲛⲍ] 'life' and begins next clause ϩⲁ[ⲟⲱⲣⲟ] 'paired-with' (cf. line 5).
ⲛⲉⲉⲧϩ likely a participial/agentive form continuing the rescue-vocabulary of line 11; sense uncertain.
Editor's restoration of the bracketed letter inside ⲟ[ⲩ]ⲁⲛ.
Standard ⲟⲩⲁⲛ ⲛⲓⲙ 'every one.'
ⲧⲍⲁⲏ ⲛⲛⲉϩⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲯ 'the end of his/its times' — eschatological idiom; cf. ⲍⲁⲏ in lines 1, 13.
Greek πάλιν 'again'; the form ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ here = ⲡⲁⲗⲓⲛ with assimilation/duplication.
1sg perfect prefix [ⲡ]ⲁⲝⲉϩ = 'I have said.'
ⲧⲛⲁ-ⲧⲥⲉⲃⲉ-ⲧⲏⲛⲉ '[I] will instruct-you'; future + causative + 2pl object suffix; symmetrical parallel to ⲁⲓ̈ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ ⲛⲏⲧⲛ in line 15.
ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the second' — parallel to ⲧⲧⲯⲁⲣⲡ (line 18), ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲯⲁⲙⲧ (line 29), ⲡⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ (line 34).
Completes ⲛ̄ⲟⲉⲣⲏⲟ ⲡⲉ 'counterpart is.'
Editor restoration; could be ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'light' or ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲉ 'manifestation' (cf. accumulated vocab).
Completes the directional ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward.'

ⲉⲧⲉⲓⲛⲉ = ⲉⲧ-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'while-bringing' (circumstantial of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'to bring/lead').
Article ⲡ- in ⲡⲉϩⲯⲛⲉ 'his soul' — formula of identification (cf. lines 4, 10, 20).
ⲭⲛ̄ = 'from'; spatial preposition pairing ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ 'the Deep' with ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height.'
ⲁⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'to the Height'; standard cosmic axis pairing with ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ. Cf. accumulated vocab.
Standard formulaic completion: 'the fourth counterpart is the spirit of darkness' — parallel to lines 18, 23, 29.

notes.decision: Page number transcribed as [ⲕⲟ] but page sequence requires ⲕⲑ (29). Treated as restoration with proposed reading ⲕⲑ; the [ⲕⲟ] in transcription may be an artifact of the same letters restoring ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ at line 1.

ⲯⲛⲉ rendered as 'soul' throughout (lines 4, 10, 19, 20, 28). Distinct from ⲯⲩⲭⲏ (the captive Living Soul) in this passage: ⲯⲛⲉ functions as the inner identifying essence of each cosmic entity (light or dark), the 'soul' that IS variously identified with spirit/light/life (light side) or fire/desire (dark side). May be a Lycopolitan native term contrasted with the Greek loan ⲯⲩⲭⲏ used here specifically of the trapped light-soul.

Greek ζωγραφία 'painting, depiction' + 'of his soul' = the cosmic Image/Painting of the Living Soul, a Manichaean technical term for the eschatological Statue/Picture of light gathered at the end. The Lycopolitan ⲛⲧⲉϩ- = 'of his.'

Translated 'is paired with' — qualitative form parallel to ⲟⲱⲗ ⲁⲍⲁⲛ 'stands beside' (accumulated vocab). The verb expresses the correspondential pairing-relation between cosmic entities (here: spirit paired with light-and-life; in dark series: king paired with the trapped soul).

ⲕⲗⲟⲟⲛⲉ rendered 'wreath' — likely Greek κλώνη/κλάδος ('branch, twig, wreath') or related to ⲕⲗⲟⲙ 'crown.' The 'wreath of light' which 'grasps within itself the five elements' is a recognizable Manichaean cosmological figure: the bound crown of light-substance.
Greek πάλιν 'again' — the doubled initial ⲧⲧ- reflects assimilation of the article/connector to the loanword. Translated 'once again.'

ⲟⲉⲣⲏⲟ = Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲟⲩ 'fellow, each-other.' Translated 'counterpart' to capture the explicit pair-structure: each of the four light counterparts is paired with a corresponding dark counterpart (lines 15-17). The numbering 'first/second/third/fourth ⲟⲉⲣⲏⲟ' enumerates members of the four-fold series.
Parsed as ⲉⲁ-ⲗⲩ-ⲱⲡⲉ = circumstantial perfect 'having become/come-to-be,' with Lycopolitan ⲗⲩ for ⲩ. 'Having come forth from the Darkness.'
ⲧⲉⲉϩ from ⲧⲱⲍ/ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, anoint, set'; here with ⲁⲝⲛ̄ 'upon' = 'who has set/poured himself upon (the soul).' The image is the dark king's intermingling with the trapped Living Soul.
Parsed as infinitive of (ⲗⲱ)ⲗⲙ̄ⲥ 'to defile, befoul' with infinitival ⲁ- and reduplication. Translated 'to defile.' The dark king pollutes the light-soul with all his powers.
'From the Deep to the Height' — the cosmic vertical axis (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ / ⲡⲭⲥⲉ). Describes the trajectory along which souls are drawn upward by the second counterpart's mechanism.
